blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Coding agents tackle successive tasks on an evolving repository, carrying forward edits and writing memory before the next task is known. Selecting memory for unknown next tasks requires balancing future usefulness against the costs of writing and reading it. The actor must also decide when acting on available memory saves effort as the task unfolds. We introduce Coding-Repository Memory (CoReMem), a cost-internalizing framework that guides memory design and actor adaptation through measured memory value on the next task. Prospective segment valuation compares runs of the next task with and without individual trajectory segments from the same inherited repository state, guiding a compact memory built around anchors: repository locations and executable checks. Actor adaptation estimates on-policy memory value within rollout groups with and without memory, using a reward that prioritizes resolution and penalizes step count in successful runs. Provenance-gated value credit assigns the additional value term to steps identified as using memory-supplied anchors, while every step retains outcome credit. On ChainSWE, CoReMem raises the 27B actor's resolve rate from 21.0% to 25.7%, with 17% fewer steps and 11% fewer total cache-aware tokens, including memory-module calls, relative to the untrained actor model without memory.

blocks.en:
In real-world software development, coding agents are expected to handle successive tasks on an
evolving repository. While prior research has primarily studied repository issues independently ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) , recent work considers sequences of tasks on a shared, evolving repository ( Jin et al., 2026 ) . We study this successive-task setting, in which tasks arrive sequentially,
each inherits the repository state left by earlier tasks, and future tasks are unknown in advance.
Since this state carries over, suitable memory can let agents reuse information acquired during
earlier exploration and avoid rediscovering it on unseen future tasks (Figure 1 ). We
therefore consider both
what a memory is worth and how an agent can use it to reduce the cost of solving unseen future
tasks.

Existing memory methods for coding agents are not specifically designed for the above successive-task
setting and do not reliably save effort (steps and tokens) on unseen future tasks
(Figure 3 ). As illustrated in Figure 2 , within-task methods learn to
compact context for the current task, whose goal is already known ( Gao et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026c ) . Most cross-task methods distill and transfer general
experience and insights across independent tasks and repositories ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2025 ) . MemOp instead accumulates memory across tasks within the same
repository, but since the repository state is reset between tasks in its setting, it optimizes its
memory design based on gains measured on the task that produced the memory ( Guo et al., 2026 ) , rather
than on its value to an unseen future task that inherits the changed repository. Given these
mismatches in setting and objective, Challenge 1 is to determine, before the future task is
known, what information is worth carrying across the task boundary .

Existing coding memory methods mainly optimize what is stored or retrieved, while typically
leaving the model that reads it unchanged ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ; Ouyang et al., 2026 ; Guo et al., 2026 ) . Yet an agent’s
information needs evolve as a task unfolds ( Zhang et al., 2023 ; Shen et al., 2026 ) , making
task-start retrieval insufficient to determine how memory should be used during execution. Challenge 2 is therefore how to use memory efficiently during execution to reduce the
cost of solving unseen future tasks on the inherited repository .

blocks.en:
To address these challenges, we introduce Co ding- Re pository Mem ory ( CoReMem ), a cost-internalizing memory framework for successive coding
tasks.
Specifically, prospective segment valuation of memory addresses Challenge 1 by first formulating
the prospective value of a memory at a task boundary, then valuing each part of the current
task’s trajectory by what it saves on the next task, and from these values inducing, through a
systematic procedure, a value-guided memory design for successive coding tasks. As a result, the
value concentrates in anchors , references to repository locations and to executable checks,
which later also mark the steps that act on the memory. To address Challenge 2, we propose on-policy adaptation for memory use with provenance-gated
value credit, which adapts the actor model itself to act on the memory where that saves effort, in
two steps. Cost-internalizing on-policy valuation trains the actor model in groups of rollouts with
the memory, without it and with a misplaced memory, under a reward that charges steps inside success,
so that the average gap between the rollouts with the memory and those without it exposes the
memory’s value to the current actor model. For the rollouts that run with the
memory, step-level provenance-gated value credit then pays the memory value to the steps whose anchors
came from the memory, so that memory use is pushed by its measured value while every step keeps its
outcome credit, and we show analytically that this push vanishes when the same value is paid to
every step.

blocks.en: 3.1 Prospective segment valuation of memory
blocks.zh: 3.1 记忆部分的预期估值

blocks.en:
To decide, before the next task is known, what to carry across a task boundary, we provide a
systematic procedure for inducing a memory design. We first define a memory’s prospective value on
the next task, and use it to find which parts of a session’s history are worth carrying because they
save effort on the next task.
blocks.zh:

blocks.en: 5 Related Work
blocks.zh: 5 相关工作

blocks.en: Coding memory spans cross-task experience ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) , within-task compression and trace validation ( Gao et al., 2026 ; Xu et al., 2026a ) ; MemOp evaluates memory through source-task replay and VibeMemBench through target-aware experience ( Guo et al., 2026 ; Fan et al., 2026a ) .

blocks.en:
Reinforcement learning trains memory construction with outcome rewards ( Wang et al., 2025b ; Yan et al., 2026c ) , refines credit through shared-state rerollouts ( Yan et al., 2026b ) and localizes it to selected turns or response tokens ( Xie et al., 2026 ; Cao et al., 2026 ) .
Our actor adaptation routes the memory’s on-policy value to provenance-marked steps on top of the outcome credit that every step keeps (§ 3.2 ).

我们的演员适应将记忆在政策上的价值引导到每个步骤所保持的结果信用之上的有出处标记的步骤(第3.2节)。

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
Memory for successive coding tasks is what one task leaves for a task it has not seen. Its worth,
measured by what the next task saves when it runs with the memory and without it, concentrates in a
few anchors, the locations and checks the next task would otherwise rediscover on its own. A memory
built around those anchors lowers the next task’s effort on six actor models, and an actor model
trained on that value, paid where it acts on them, lowers effort further without lowering resolution.
blocks.zh:
连续编码任务的内存是它没有看到的任务留下的。 它的价值,
以下一个任务运行时所保存的内存和没有内存来衡量,集中在一个
很少锚,地点和检查 下一个任务 否则会重新发现自己。 一个记忆
围绕这些地标建造的 降低了下一个任务的努力 在六个演员模型, 和一个演员模型
接受过关于这一价值的培训,在对其采取行动时支付,进一步降低努力,而不降低分辨率。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
Our main experiments use Python repositories in the mini-swe-agent harness, and post-training covers
the three open-weight actor models. Other programming languages and larger actor models
remain to be tested. We measure effort by steps and cache-aware tokens and do not report wall-clock
latency or energy use. How memory should be accumulated and refreshed over longer repository
histories is future work.
blocks.zh:
我们的主要实验是使用Python寄存器 在迷你Swe-Agent的牵引, 和训练后盖
三个露天演员模特 其他编程语言和较大的演员模式
还有待测试。 我们用步骤和缓存符号衡量努力,不报告时钟
延迟或能量使用。 如何积累和刷新较长的存储器
历史是未来的工作。

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en:
This work uses publicly released benchmarks, built from open-source repositories, and models in
accordance with their licenses, and involves no human participants. Every agent session runs inside
the per-task container image of its benchmark. In deployment, a cross-task memory may retain
repository content such as file paths, commands and test output, so in private repositories it should
follow the repository’s access control and retention policy, with secrets redacted before storage. As
plain text, the memory can be audited and deleted.
blocks.zh:
这项工作使用公开发布的基准,由开源寄存器和模型构建于
并且没有涉及任何人类参与者。 每个代理会话都在内部运行
其基准的每个任务容器图像。 在部署时,可保留跨任务记忆
文件路径、命令和测试输出等寄存器内容, 因此在私人寄存器中它应该
遵循存储器的访问控制和保存政策,在存储前修改机密。 作为
纯文本,内存可以审核并删除.

memory in context. This alternative is related to context attribution ( Cohen-Wang et al., 2024 ) and to probability contrasts used in context-aware decoding ( Shi et al., 2024 ) and

message content. A flat ratio next to a sharp anchor match says that the memory changes a few actions
rather than conditioning the whole distribution, which is why the credit signal is provenance and not
likelihood.

blocks.en:
Each step of a trajectory is an assistant message, made of reasoning text and a shell command, followed by the
output of that command. The command goes to the commands segment together with the exit code of its
step, and the output goes to one segment by what produced it, under rules fixed before the study (the
first match wins). Output of a command that prints a diff ( git diff , git show , a
patch file) goes to the change segment; output of a test runner ( pytest , tox , unittest and the like), of a script written in the session or of inline Python that contains an assert goes to the test segment; all other output goes to the repository segment, including
that of linters such as flake8 , which the list does not name. The change the task left in the tree joins
the change segment. The outcome and the scratch files come from the boundary, not from the transcript,
and harness format messages ( 0.05 % 0.05\% of the material) are left out. Each segment is cut to a fixed
quota ( 4,000 4{,}000 characters, 200 200 for the outcome and 800 800 for scratch files), so a segment is the same
text in every arm that contains it. None of these assignments reads what the text says, since each
segment is read off what the harness records, the assistant message, the command and its exit code,
its output, the diff and the end of the session. Table 7 defines the seven segments
with an example from one real session, shown in Figure 9 .

blocks.en:
This appendix records how each line of the CoReMem memory was obtained from the raw session, and where
each decision came from. The derivation ran in five steps. The first three are mechanical, the fourth
arranges the fields into the memory’s two blocks, and the fifth validates the result. Table 8 maps every segment measurement to the line it produced.

本附录记录了CoReMem内存的每行是如何从生会话中获取的,以及在哪里获取的.
每一个决定都来自。 引出分五步而行. 前三个是机械的,第四个
将字段排列入记忆的两个块,第五个块验证结果. 表8将每个段的测量图都映射到它所产生的行.

blocks.en:
The current task’s session is split by the role each piece of text plays,
namely the agent’s reasoning (C1), the commands it issued (C2), the repository content it read (C3), the
feedback of its tests (C4), the change it left (C5), its outcome (C6) and its scratch files (C7). The
outcome segment is cut in two, the outcome the writer can observe and the verdict of the hidden tests,
and the latter may never enter a memory. Three compressed forms are added as probes, the failing commands
with their output, the diff’s file list, and the test commands with their exit codes but no output.

当前的任务会议由每个文本的作用分成,

blocks.en:
Definition 1 is implemented as a string matcher, the same one that marks memory-driven
steps in § 3.2.2 . A text is split into tokens, and a token is an anchor when it falls into
one of the four kinds of Table 9 . Three filters keep generic strings out. Tokens
shorter than six characters are dropped, as are tokens whose every part is a common English or shell
word ( command-line , pytest ), and scaffolding found in nearly every repository
( setup.py , conftest.py , reproduce.py and paths under /tmp ). A path:lines reference is matched on its path, so the line range in a memory guides the next task
without being required for a match. For provenance (Eq. ( 6 )) the memory’s anchors are further
reduced to those absent from the session so far and from what the memory-free sessions of the same
group reach in their first eight steps.

blocks.en:
This section sets out the alternatives to three design choices and what the paper’s own measurements
say about them.
blocks.zh:
本节列出三种设计选择的替代办法以及纸张本身的测量方法
说说他们

blocks.en:
A separate reader, or a retrieval policy, decides what memory to hand the actor, either before the task
or between its steps. In our setting the memory is short, at most ten lines, and already sits in the
actor’s context, so the open question is not which memory to show but whether and when the actor acts
on it. Which steps use the memory emerges as the task unfolds. What a coding agent needs is often not
evident from the task description and surfaces as it explores and executes, so a single retrieval
keyed on the task input falls short of multi-step repository exploration ( Trivedi et al., 2023 ; Yang et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2026a ) , retrieval from the unfinished code alone misses what a draft
reveals ( Zhang et al., 2023 ) , and memory retrieved per subtask during execution outperforms memory
retrieved by whole-task similarity ( Shen et al., 2026 ) . Under the detector that training uses,
credited steps concentrate late in a trajectory, where the actor runs the tests the memory names, while
early steps that match the memory are mostly steps the actor takes without any memory
(App. G ). A reader that selects memory up front cannot see this, and a reader that
re-selects at every step would need the same per-step signal we give the actor. We therefore adapt the
actor itself and pay the measured value to the steps that use the memory. Retrieval stays compatible
with this choice, since a retrieval policy decides what memory enters the context and the adaptation
changes what the actor does with it.
Related controllers decide when to inject reminders (PMA; Wu et al., 2026 ), whether to retrieve
or abstain (RSCB-MC; Iscan, 2026 ), and how to navigate memory at different granularities
(NapMem; Xu et al., 2026b ). These choices concern memory access, whereas our update targets
execution after a short memory is already present.

A separate memory model leaves the actor untouched but cannot change how it acts on memory, and full
fine-tuning can move the actor’s general coding behaviour. A LoRA adapter on frozen base weights is the
middle ground, a low-rank update that bounds how far the actor moves while letting it adapt its use of
memory. Whether general capability survives is a measurement, not a property of the adapter. On
SWE-bench Verified, with no memory in context, the adapted 27B and 9B actors resolve 4.5 4.5 and 6.4 6.4 points more than their untrained counterparts with 7 % 7\% and 22 % 22\% fewer steps
(Table 4 ), so on this benchmark the adaptation cost no general capability.

blocks.en:
Agent memory encompasses reflective feedback and extracted experience ( Shinn et al., 2023 ; Zhao et al., 2024 ) ,
reusable workflows and executable skills ( Wang et al., 2025c ; Wang et al., 2024 ) , and adaptive
inference-time experience ( Suzgun et al., 2025 ; Tang et al., 2025 ) .
Other systems organize episodic or conversational information through reflection, retrieval, memory
hierarchies and linked records ( Park et al., 2023 ; Zhong et al., 2024 ; Packer et al., 2023 ; Xu et al., 2025 ) .
MemOS and EverMemOS address memory organization and lifecycle management ( Li et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2026 ) ; Zhang et al. (2024) survey the broader design space.
blocks.zh:
物剂记忆包括反射反馈和取出的经验(Shinn等,2023;Zhao等,2024),
可重复使用的工作流程和可执行的技能(Wang等,2025c;Wang等,2024),以及适应性
推断时间经验 (Suzgun等,2025;Tang等,2025.).
其他系统通过反射,检索,内存来组织静脉或对话信息.
等级和关联记录(Park等,2023;Zhong等,2024;Packer等,2023;Xu等,2025).
MemOS和EverMemOS地址为内存组织和生命周期管理(Li等,2025;Hu等,2026;); 张等 (2024)勘测更广阔的设计空间.

blocks.en:
Memory systems keep different forms of experience: Mem0 extracts facts from conversations ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) , ReasoningBank and SWE-Exp distill lessons from past trajectories ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2025 ) , Repository Memory and MemCoder mine commit history for localization and development knowledge ( Wang et al., 2026 ; Deng et al., 2026b ) , and MemOp maintains a per-repository guidebook with a trained writer ( Guo et al., 2026 ) .
These approaches emphasize retained experience or repository knowledge; our setting additionally
carries the actual edited repository state.
AdaRepair-Mem selects repair experience by coverage, quality and repair stage ( Luo et al., 2026b ) .
Repository context files also require empirical evaluation: AGENTS.md studies find that added
instructions need not improve success and can increase cost ( Gloaguen et al., 2026 ) .
Persistent project information appears in deployed assistants through Claude Code’s auto memory and
Codex’s cross-session memory generation and injection ( Anthropic, 2026a ; OpenAI, 2026a ) .
Within one task, SWE-MeM and CompactionRL learn context compression jointly with issue resolution ( Gao et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026c ) , and the concurrent MemTrace re-validates stored execution traces against the evolving repository ( Xu et al., 2026a ) ; these memories do not outlive the task.
CAMG-RL likewise learns file-based memory operations across context boundaries within an
episode ( Luo et al., 2026a ) .
Between the two lies the boundary a deployed agent meets, a memory written before the next task is known and read in the repository state the last task left.
blocks.zh:

blocks.en:
LoCoMo and LongMemEval test long-term conversational memory ( Maharana et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2025 ) ,
StateMemBench tests evolving-state tracking ( Fan et al., 2026b ) , and MemoryArena couples memory
with interdependent multi-session actions ( He et al., 2026 ) .
LongCodeBench evaluates long-context code comprehension and repair ( Rando et al., 2025 ) .
These settings probe memory retention and use, while our evaluation measures the effort saved on an
unseen coding task from inherited repository state.

blocks.en:
SWE-bench grades each issue from its own snapshot ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) , whereas ChainSWE chains fixes in a shared workspace ( Jin et al., 2026 ) and SWE-Milestone reports resolve falling from above 80% to 38% once state is carried ( Deng et al., 2026a ) ; SWEContextBench and Handoff Debt study reuse across related issues and the cost of resuming an interrupted one ( Zhu et al., 2026 ; KC and Budathoki, 2026 ) .
Memory-specific evaluations isolate the retained information: MemOp reruns the source task with and without a candidate memory ( Guo et al., 2026 ) , VibeMemBench pairs memory-off and memory-on runs of one target whose history is summarised with the target in view ( Fan et al., 2026a ) , and Decision-Aware Memory Cards score evidence by a heuristic estimate of its effect on the next action ( Guan et al., 2026 ) .
Related proxies include interventions on candidate memories for answer quality ( Srivastava, 2026 ) ,
answer-conditioned information gain ( Han et al., 2026 ) , and Shapley-based context filtering for code
completion ( Huo et al., 2026 ) . MemDelta emphasizes controlled model and retrieval comparisons
and write-path cost accounting ( Wang, 2026 ) .
These evaluations complement our paired runs of an unseen next task from the inherited tree,
which measure resolution and effort and attribute savings to trajectory segments (§ 3.1 ).

blocks.en:
Reinforcement learning has been applied to both sides of the memory interface.
Writers are trained from outcome reward or neighbourhood-level marginal utility ( Wang et al., 2025b ; Yan et al., 2026c ; Ye et al., 2026 ) , with finer credit from rerolling at a shared memory state ( Yan et al., 2026b ) , hindsight-filtered utility on writing tokens ( Yan et al., 2026a ) , or token-level attribution ( Li et al., 2026a ) ; RoMeRL notes the outcome-broadcast trap but treats paired rollouts as infeasible ( Yang et al., 2026 ) .
On the reading side, ECHO routes outcome credit to the turns a policy selects back into context ( Xie et al., 2026 ) , and MemCalib localises credit by atom ablation ( Cao et al., 2026 ) .
End-to-end memory learning also includes recurrent consolidation in MEM1 ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) ,
chunk-wise processing in MemAgent ( Yu et al., 2025 ) , self-memory policies in MemPO ( Li et al., 2026b ) ,
and operation-tree credit in Mem-T ( Yue et al., 2026 ) .
These methods optimize different memory interfaces and credit granularities. Our contribution pairs
on-policy valuation on executable next tasks with provenance-gated routing of the additional
memory-value term, while retaining outcome credit at every step (§ 3.2 ).

blocks.en:
Classical RL assigns hindsight credit to past actions ( Harutyunyan et al., 2019 ) or uses
counterfactual baselines to separate action contributions ( Foerster et al., 2018 ; Mesnard et al., 2021 ) .
For language models, process supervision supplies intermediate labels ( Lightman et al., 2024 ) ,
VinePPO estimates step values with sampled continuations ( Kazemnejad et al., 2025 ) ,
GiGPO groups repeated states for local advantages ( Feng et al., 2025 ) , and C3 replays downstream
continuations after message interventions in agent teams ( Chen et al., 2026 ) .
These methods address action or message utility; our provenance gate identifies traceable memory
use and routes measured memory value without estimating each step’s causal effect.

blocks.en:
SWE-Gym and SWE-smith expand executable training tasks and agent trajectories ( Pan et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2025 ) ,
while SWE-RL trains on software-evolution data ( Wei et al., 2025 ) .
SWE-Edit reduces overhead through editing-interface decomposition ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) ;
L1 and efficient-reasoning RL shape generation length and inference compute ( Aggarwal and Welleck, 2025 ; Arora and Zanette, 2025 ) .
These approaches complement our focus on information reuse and memory use across task boundaries.
